meta.title: Ezequiel Ranieri — Backend & Security Engineer
meta.description: Backend & Security Engineer working in Go: Linux, IAM, PostgreSQL and row-level security, distributed systems and systems security. Long-term direction: Trusted AI Infrastructure.

blog.subtitle: Engineering notes on backend and security

howIWork.subtitle: Backend and security engineering, with a long-term focus on trusted AI infrastructure

securityFirst.name: Security First
securityFirst.text: Threat modeling from day 0. Capability-based security, zero-trust, least privilege by default.

hexagonalArchitecture.name: Hexagonal Architecture
hexagonalArchitecture.text: Pure domain with zero external dependencies. Ports & adapters for DB, HTTP, gRPC, OIDC.

testingAsSpecification.name: Isolation by Default
testingAsSpecification.text: Tenant isolation enforced in the database with RLS FORCE. Untrusted code runs sandboxed in WASM with metered fuel.

nativeObservability.name: Verifiable by Construction
nativeObservability.text: Signed receipts and hash-chained audit. Every agent action leaves verifiable proof.

simplicityOverCleverness.name: Evaluate Before You Trust
simplicityOverCleverness.text: Declarative specs, authorization oracles and regression gates in CI. Agent behavior is tested, not assumed.

livingDocumentation.name: Living Documentation
livingDocumentation.text: ADRs for architectural decisions. README as entry point. Comments only for "why", never "what".

items.exploreFirst: I explore first: I understand the existing code, constraints and trade-offs before proposing anything
items.specifyExplicitly: I specify explicitly: ADRs for irreversible decisions, specs for features
items.implementInVerticalSlices: I build in vertical slices: every commit delivers verifiable value
items.verifyAutomatically: I verify automatically: tests, linter, type-check and security scan in CI
items.reviewWithJudgment: I review with judgment: deep review for medium/high risk, structural review for low-risk changes
items.deliverInWorkUnitCommits: I ship per unit of work: tests, docs and code together, Conventional Commits
